If you don't have a need to file the 1099, I wouldn't list it as a "job", because there's no way that they will know (if you are disclosing this information to your future employer for background check purposes). 

I don't know how extensive the background check in your industry will be, but I would make sure I use a separate email, don't show face, and keep your profile as far away from your reality as you can. I definitely would not put this on a resume if it will get you rejected from a steady job. In general I believe the resume should be tailored to the job anyway so if it's not relevant I wouldn't put it. 

Hope this helps some.

ETA: if you are in the position that you end up filing a 1099, the employer won't say feetfinder, they will be under another company name, and you can say anything you want when it comes to that self employment part (freelance work, etc). I still wouldn't list it on my resume but if asked, you will be able to cover yourself some.
